extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (research mathematicians and computational algebra practitioners using SINGULAR libraries)
extracted.subtask_description: API reference / procedure documentation for several SINGULAR libraries (finitediff.lib, goettsche.lib, graal.lib, gitfan.lib). Lists usage, input types, return types, purpose, notes, and examples for each procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: errormap
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: errormap(f); f of type poly. Return type: poly; performs the fouriertransformation of a single polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows preparing finitediff.lib, setinitials and a scheme, then calling errormap on a scheme expression; output illustrated. (No additional notes beyond usage/example.)

rubrics_metrics.name: matrixsystem
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: matrixsystem(M,A); where M = Mt,M1,..,Mn is a list with square matrices of the same dimension as entries, and A = At,A1,..,An gives the corresponding approximations as vector. Intended to solve Mt*U_t + M1*U_x1 + .. + Mn*U_xn = 0 as a linear system of PDEs numerically via finite difference scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return type: matrix; gives back matrices B1,B2 that represent the finite difference scheme partitioned into different time levels in form B1*U(t=N)=B2*U(t<N), where N is maximal occurring degree (timelevel) of t. Example provided using finitediff.lib showing resulting matrix entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: timestep
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: timestep(M); M a square matrix with polynomials over the basering as entries. Return type: list; gives two matrices M1,M2 that are the splitting of M with respect to the degree of variable t in the entries, where M1 consists of polynomials of the highest timelevel and M2 of the lower levels in the form M1-M2=M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: intended to be used for finite-difference-scheme-construction and partition into time steps. Example shows calling timestep on output of matrixsystem and printed split matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: fouriersystem
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: fouriersystem(M,A); M a list of matrices, A a list of approximations. Return type: list; each entry is a matrix obtained by substituting the single approximations into the system of PDEs, partitioning into several timesteps and Fourier-transforming these parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example using finitediff.lib demonstrates calling fouriersystem with matrices and approximations and shows various matrix outputs (transformed expressions).

rubrics_metrics.name: PartitionVar
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PartitionVar(f); f a poly in the basering. Return type: poly; gives back a list L = f1,f2 obtained by the partition of f into two parts f1,f2 with deg_var_n(f1) > 0 and deg_var_n(f2) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates setinitials and partitioning a polynomial into the part depending on a specified variable and the constant-in-that-variable part; basering and parameter/variable context shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: ComplexValue
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ComplexValue(f); f a poly in the basering. Return type: poly; gives back the formal complex-value of f, where var(1) is regarded as the imaginary unit. Only makes sense if <setinitials> executed before (nvars <= npars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows ComplexValue applied after errormap and other transforms producing polynomial where var(1) treated as imaginary unit; printed transformed polynomial provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: VarToPar
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: VarToPar(f); f a poly in the basering. Return type: poly; returns the polynomial obtained by substituting var(i) by par(i) for all variables. Only makes sense if <setinitials> executed before (nvars <= npars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows VarToPar converting variables into parameters in a polynomial after setinitials; basering and parameter list context provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: ParToVar
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ParToVar(f); f a poly in the basering. Return type: poly; returns the polynomial obtained by substituting par(i) by var(i) for the first nvars(basering) parameters. Only makes sense if setinitials executed before (nvars <= npars). This is the inverse action to VarToPar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows round-trip VarToPar then ParToVar producing original polynomial (comparison h == f yields 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: qepcad
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: qepcad(f); f a poly in the basering. Return type: list; gives back some constraints that are equivalent to f < 1 (computed by QEPCAD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows preparing a polynomial, calling qepcad, and that system-level QEPCAD commands may be missing (error messages shown). Output may be numeric constraints or errors if external commands missing; note 'Try manually' in example.

rubrics_metrics.name: qepcadsystem
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: qepcadsystem(f); l a list. Return: list. Purpose: gives back some constraints that are equivalent to the eigenvalues of the matrices in the list l being < 1 (computed by QEPCAD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows using fouriersystem output then calling qepcadsystem on a matrix list; example shows system errors when external QEPCAD tool not found and suggests manual try.

rubrics_metrics.name: GoettscheF
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GoettscheF(z, t, n, b); z, t polynomials, n integer, b list of non-negative integers. Return: polynomial in z and t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes Goettsche’s formula up to degree n in t. Note: returns zero if n<0 or b is not a list of non-negative integers or if there are not enough Betti numbers. Example computing formula for projective plane Betti numbers provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPolyH
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PPolyH(z, n, b); z polynomial, n integer, b list of non-negative integers. Return: polynomial in z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes the Poincare polynomial of the Hilbert scheme of n points on a surface with Betti numbers b. Note: returns zero if n<0 or b invalid or insufficient Betti numbers. Example for P2 given.

rubrics_metrics.name: BettiNumsH
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: BettiNumsH(n, b); n integer, b list of non-negative integers. Return: list of non-negative integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes the Betti numbers of the Hilbert scheme of n points on a surface with Betti numbers b. Note: returns empty list if n<0 or b invalid or insufficient Betti numbers. Example shows printed list entries for P2, n=3.

rubrics_metrics.name: MacdonaldF
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: MacdonaldF(z, t, n, b); z, t polynomials, n integer, b list of non-negative integers. Return: polynomial in z and t with integer coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes Macdonald’s formula up to degree n in t. Note: returns zero if n<0 or b invalid. Example for projective plane shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPolyS
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PPolyS(z, n, b); z polynomial, n integer, b list of non-negative integers. Return: polynomial in z with integer coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes the Poincare polynomial of the n-th symmetric power of a variety with Betti numbers b. Note: returns zero if n<0 or b invalid. Example for P2 symmetric power shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: BettiNumsS
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: BettiNumsS(n, b); n integer, b list of non-negative integers. Return: list of non-negative integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes the Betti numbers of the n-th symmetric power of a variety with Betti numbers b. Note: returns empty list if n<0 or b invalid. Examples include elliptic curve and P2.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPolyN
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PPolyN(t, q, m, n); t polynomial, q, m, n integers. Return: polynomial in t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes the Poincare polynomial of the moduli space of Kronecker modules N(q; m, n). Note: if m and n are not coprime the result does not necessarily make sense. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: BettiNumsN
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: BettiNumsN(q, m, n); q, m, n integers. Return: list of integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes the Betti numbers of the moduli space of Kronecker modules N(q; m, n). Note: if m and n are not coprime the result may not make sense. Example for N(3;2,3) provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: graalMixed
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: graalMixed(L, t); L ideal, t int (optional). Return: graalBearer with all necessary structures for the graal machinery if t specified and t>0 (t sets an upper time limit on finding a necessary transformation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: assumes current basering is a domain and L is a prime ideal. Purpose: yields structures for computational treatment of localizations at prime ideals and associated graded rings. Example given referencing Mora and showing the graalBearer contents and mappings.

rubrics_metrics.name: dimensionOfLocalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dimensionOfLocalization(L); L ideal or graalBearer. Return: int, the dimension of the localization A_L of A at L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates constructing qring, graalBearer via graalMixed and calling dimensionOfLocalization(Gr) returning dimension (example: 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: systemOfParametersOfLocalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: systemOfParametersOfLocalization(def L); L ideal or graalBearer. Return: ideal, a system of parameters of the localization A_L of A at L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows obtaining the system of parameters from a graalBearer; includes note that L may be adapted (redefining J etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: isLocalizationRegular
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isLocalizationRegular(def L); L ideal or graalBearer. Return: int, 1 if the localization A_L is regular, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates calling isLocalizationRegular(Gr) returning 1 in that example.

rubrics_metrics.name: warkedPreimageStd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: warkedPreimageStd(wM); wM is a warkedModule containing specified components (wM.Gr graalBearer, wM.modQ0y generating set, wM.stdmodQ0y empty, wM.qQ0y empty, wM.modKy corresponding generating set, wM.stdmodKy empty, wM.qKy empty, wM.w weights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: the same warkedModule except populated fields: stdmodQ0y contains subset G for standard basis lifting, qQ0y a transformation matrix, stdmodKy a standard basis of modKy, qKy a transformation matrix. Standard basis of modAy computed by lifting a Groebner basis of modKy. Example shows building wM, calling warkedPreimageStd and printed standard basis results.

rubrics_metrics.name: resolutionInLocalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: resolutionInLocalization(I, L); I ideal, L ideal or graalBearer. Purpose: compute the resolution of I * A_L where A_L is the localization of the current basering (possibly quotient ring) at a prime ideal L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a marked resolution object. Example demonstrates computing a (possibly non-minimal) resolution, then localizing and calling resolutionInLocalization with a graalBearer; includes note that full resolution in a qring may be infinite and a max length may be set. Example output shows resolution over Al and Graal with printed maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: isAface
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isAface(a, gam0); a: ideal, gam0: intvec. Purpose: checks whether gam0 is an a-face with respect to the ideal a. Return: int (0 or 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates calling isAface on simple ideals and intvecs and expected results (0 or 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: afaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: afaces(a [, L]); a: ideal, L: list of intvecs (optional). Purpose: returns a list of all a-faces (as intvecs of 0/1 where i-th entry is 1 if the cone has the i-th unit basis vector as generator). If L specified only faces of simplex listed in L are considered (useful for representatives wrt group action). Return: list of intvecs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show computing afaces for various ideals including zero ideal and more complex ideals; print(size(F)) used to show counts. Note suitable for use with symmetry-reduced lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: fullDimImages
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: fullDimImages(afaces, Q); afaces: list, Q: intmat. Purpose: determines which a-faces (intvecs) in the list have a full-dimensional projection with respect to Q. Return: list of intvecs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates filtering a list of afaces with a given Q matrix and showing sizes before/after filtering.

rubrics_metrics.name: minimalAfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minimalAfaces(listOfAfaces); listOfAfaces: list (must only contain a-faces which project to full dimension). Purpose: returns list of all minimal a-faces. Return: list of intvecs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows pipeline afaces -> fullDimImages -> minimalAfaces with sizes at each stage; setcores may be used to set parallel cores prior.

rubrics_metrics.name: orbitCones
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: orbitCones(AF, Q[, d]); AF: list of intvecs, Q: intmat, d: int (optional). Purpose: returns list consisting of all cones Q(gam0) where gam0 in AF. If d is given returns only orbit cones of dimension at least d. Return: list of cones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows calling orbitCones on AF and Q and printing size of returned list; used as intermediate step for GIT fan computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: GITcone
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GITcone(OCcones, w); OCcones: list of orbit cones, w: bigintmat with one row. Purpose: returns the intersection of all orbit cones containing w. Return: cone, intvec with the GIT cone containing w, and the hash of this cone (indices of orbit cones contributing to the intersection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs AF->fullDimImages->minimalAfaces->orbitCones and a weight vector w, then calls GITcone which prints AMBIENT_DIM, FACETS, LINEAR_SPAN and contributing orbit-cone indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: GITfan
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GITfan(J, Q [, G]); J: ideal, Q: intmat, G: list (optional symmetry group). Purpose: computes the GIT fan associated to J and Q, optionally using a symmetry group action on the column space of Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a fan, the GIT fan. Notes: procedure uses parallel computation for construction of GIT-cones; a-faces are not computed in parallel (can call aface with simplex faces). If used with optional G, orbit decomposition of simplex of columns of Q is computed; example shows setcores(4) before running and passing simplexSymmetryGroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: GITfanFromOrbitCones
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GITfanFromOrbitCones(OC, Q, Qgamma [, file1, file2]); OC: list of orbit cones, Q: bigintmat, Qgamma: cone, optional file names. Purpose: returns common refinement of cones in OC (supposed to contain orbit cones intersected with Qgamma). Return: list containing bigint hashes of GIT cones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional file1/file2 can store hashes and H-representation cones. Example shows constructing AF->OC, forming Qgamma as coneViaPoints(transpose(Q)), calling this function and printing size of returned list (example: 76).

rubrics_metrics.name: GITfanParallel
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GITfanParallel(OC, Q, Qgamma [, file1]); OC: list, Q: intmat, Qgamma: cone, file1: string (optional). Purpose: returns the common refinement of cones given in OC (orbit cones intersected with Qgamma) using parallel computation for construction of GIT-cones. Return: list containing bigint hashes of GIT cones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: uses parallel computation. Example shows setcores(4), building AF->OC->Qgamma and calling GITfanParallel returning list of GIT-cone hashes (example size: 76).
